historical_novelty_guard.reason: Ketan Mulmuley's GCT/Flip literature explicitly discusses and formalizes a self-referential paradox in P vs NP; other informal uses of the phrase P-vs-NP paradox also exist.
historical_novelty_guard.candidate_novelty: A precisely frozen finite resource phenomenon in which an exact Boolean/algebraic coordinate compression lowers semantic dimension while increasing the explicit proof-carrying CNF representation volume under a fixed cap.

central_candidate.name: JANUS Algebraic Compression / Proof-Volume Paradox
central_candidate.statement: An exact algebraic/Boolean coordinate change can strictly reduce the number of semantic degrees of freedom while strictly increasing the size of the explicit proof-carrying representation required by the chosen proof language.
central_candidate.frozen_equation: Delta semantic dimension = -1 while Delta certified state volume = +354 (241 -> 595), with Phi 13 -> 12 but cap 256 violated.

nodes.name: JANUS Algebraic Compression / Proof-Volume Paradox
nodes.core_tension: semantic dimension decreases while proof representation volume increases
nodes.evidence: PHP_5_4_C1 direct block-coordinate witness: 13->12 variables, Phi 13->12, state_units 241->595

nodes.name: JANUS Add-to-Subtract Extension Paradox
nodes.core_tension: one introduces a new extension variable in order to eliminate old variables, but the intermediate representation may become harder to eliminate than the original one
nodes.evidence: selector e<->(b OR c) fits at 251 units, yet first exact elimination of b or c does not fit under 256

nodes.name: JANUS Certificate-Materialization Paradox
nodes.core_tension: a compact certificate can describe a global structure whose explicit materialization violates the resource cap
nodes.evidence: S4 orbit has a tiny generator description, while materializing four selectors reaches 281>256

nodes.name: JANUS Orbit-Quotient Paradox
nodes.core_tension: exact automorphism symmetry does not by itself justify quotienting distinct variables or states
nodes.evidence: 24/24 S4 block permutations preserve the residual, but quotient/materialization still requires proof-carrying semantics and bounded representation

nodes.name: JANUS Extension-Debt Paradox
nodes.core_tension: local compression opens legal eliminations while preserving the global live-variable debt
nodes.evidence: M1->E1->M2->E2 opens 248 second eliminations, but +1 macro/-1 old variable keeps Phi at 13; 496 cleanup attempts give zero fits

nodes.name: JANUS Parrondo Composition Paradox
nodes.core_tension: two individually stalled transformations can become productive when alternated, without guaranteeing global progress
nodes.evidence: without recompression second-elimination fits=0; with M2 recompression second-elimination fits=248; third progress remains blocked

nodes.name: JANUS Discovery-Verification Paradox
nodes.core_tension: a certificate may be polynomially cheap to verify while discovering the right certificate can contain the original hard search problem
nodes.evidence: JECC/B2 gate requires deterministic polynomial macro discovery in addition to polynomial replay

nodes.name: JANUS Proof-Language Paradox
nodes.core_tension: the same contradiction can be exponentially hard in one proof language and polynomially short in a stronger language
nodes.historical_anchor: Haken: PHP exponential for Resolution; Extended Resolution has polynomial proofs

nodes.name: JANUS Residual-Quotient Paradox
nodes.core_tension: many syntactic residuals can collapse to a tiny exact quotient on structured families, while general semantic equivalence testing can encode UNSAT/coNP difficulty

nodes.name: JANUS Akinator Question-Cost Paradox
nodes.core_tension: a polynomial number of exact questions can locate a solution, while answering each globally useful question may hide NP/#P hardness

nodes.name: JANUS Braess Extension Paradox
nodes.core_tension: adding an apparently helpful representational edge/variable can worsen the global resource state
nodes.historical_anchor: Braess paradox: adding a network edge can worsen equilibrium travel cost

nodes.name: JANUS Simpson Progress Paradox
nodes.core_tension: local progress metrics can improve while the aggregate/global progress measure remains flat or reverses
nodes.historical_anchor: Simpson's paradox: aggregated and stratified trends can reverse

nodes.name: JANUS Berry-Chaitin Compression Paradox
nodes.core_tension: short descriptions can define objects whose minimal-description or incompressibility properties are not uniformly computable/certifiable

nodes.name: JANUS Skolem Size Paradox
nodes.core_tension: size can depend on the representational/model perspective; semantic smallness in one coordinate system need not imply smallness of the internal proof representation
nodes.historical_anchor: Skolem's paradox: countability is relative to the model

nodes.name: JANUS Banach-Tarski Orbit Paradox
nodes.core_tension: group action and decomposition can make global structure radically different from naive volume intuition
nodes.historical_anchor: Banach-Tarski paradox and paradoxical decompositions under group actions

nodes.name: JANUS Mahaney Sparsity-Collapse Paradox
nodes.core_tension: if NP-hard information could be represented in a sufficiently sparse NP-complete set under polynomial many-one reductions, P would equal NP

nodes.name: JANUS Instance-Compression Collapse Paradox
nodes.core_tension: too powerful a uniform compression of OR-SAT instances would force NP into coNP/poly and collapse PH

nodes.name: JANUS Relativization Mirror Paradox
nodes.core_tension: the same relativizing proof style is compatible with oracle worlds where P=NP and worlds where P!=NP

nodes.name: JANUS Natural-Proof Barrier Paradox
nodes.core_tension: a broad constructive property strong enough to separate general circuits can conflict with the assumed existence of strong pseudorandom functions

nodes.name: JANUS Algebrization Barrier Paradox
nodes.core_tension: even techniques that escape ordinary relativization can still remain too invariant under algebraic oracle extensions to resolve central separations

nodes.name: GCT Flip / Explicit-Proof Self-Reference
nodes.core_tension: hardness proofs themselves should admit explicit proof certificates that are easy to verify, construct and decode
nodes.historical_anchor: Ketan Mulmuley, GCT Flip, JACM 2011 / Explicit Proofs and The Flip 2010

nodes.name: JANUS Blum-Speedup Solver Paradox
nodes.core_tension: for some computable functions there is no asymptotically optimal algorithm; every candidate can be improved

master_principle.name: JANUS Compression Self-Collapse Principle
master_principle.statement: The more uniformly and exactly an NP-hard search space can be compressed with polynomial-time discoverable, polynomial-size, polynomially verifiable certificates and a strictly decreasing polynomially bounded global potential, the closer the compression mechanism itself is to being the polynomial-time solver.
